doc.description:
The raw textual documentation associated with this piece of metadata. This will have the original comment
characters removed, but otherwise be a simple block of text with the original formatting retained. Only
documentation comments (starting with `/**`) will be used for this purpose and only when immediately
preceding the structure they document.

default.description:
The value expression passed if the argument is unspecified by the caller. Use #defaultValue to get the
"evaluated" value.

If the value type of the parameter is a named enum, the default should be the label (field name) from the enum
type or an expression that evaluates to one.

@see #defaultValue

title:
Each formal parameter to a function has a name and value type, and may also have annotations. Parameters have
various options:
 - non empty: must specify a non-null / non-empty argument when calling
 - optional: may be completely omitted
 - default: value used if argument is not specified when calling
 - this: special parameter indicating the instance on which the method is being called

```type
type Example {
  nonEmpty:    function(x: !string)
  nonOptional: function(x: !?string)
  optional:    function(x: string)
  default:     function(x: string = 'kittens')
}
```

In the example above, `nonEmpty` cannot be called without specifying the argument; nor may the argument be null or
an empty string. This the the strongest constraint and most common modifier.

`nonOptional` cannot be called without specifying the argument, but the value specified may be null or empty string.

`optional` can be called with or without specifying the argument and null will be received by the method if not.

`default` can be called without specifying the argument, in which case the method will receive the default value.

@see FunctionType
